headline_hook: GPT-5.6 Goes Invite-Only as Asian Labs Ship Frontier Rivals

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The Sol/Terra/Luna naming isn't marketing theater — it's OpenAI hardcoding a permanent product hierarchy that tells you more about their enterprise strategy than any capabilities announcement ever could.

model_literacy.relevance: GLM 5.2 beating Claude on Semgrep's cyber benchmarks while trailing on general evals shows why single-number leaderboards are misleading — the models that matter are the ones that win on YOUR task, not MMLU.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Splits Into Sol, Terra, and Luna — Access Is the New Moat
items.angle: The tiered naming signals a permanent product hierarchy: frontier capability is no longer something you ship to everyone, it's something you ration by trust level.
items.key_fact: Restricted to trusted partners only — no public API access at launch

items.title: A Developer Used Claude Code to Get a Second Opinion on His MRI
items.angle: Not a medical startup pitch — a solo developer feeding DICOM files into an LLM and getting actionable analysis. The 418 RTs tell you how many people want this.
items.key_fact: 308 HN likes, 418 retweets — massive engagement on medical AI use case

items.title: Apple's Vision Pro Chief Jumps Ship to OpenAI's Hardware Team
items.angle: When Apple's spatial computing VP leaves for an AI lab's hardware division, you're watching the next device form factor get designed in real time.
items.key_fact: Paul Meade, VP of Vision Pro, joining OpenAI hardware

items.title: Simon Willison Resurfaces Jon Udell's Thinking on AI Tooling
items.angle: Udell has been mapping developer tool paradigms for decades — his AI tooling perspective carries historical pattern-matching most hot-takes lack.
items.key_fact: Published via Willison's link blog, connecting decades of developer tool thinking to AI

items.title: Asian Startups Ship Mythos-Class Models While US Export Bans Hold Anthropic Back
items.angle: Export restrictions designed to maintain US AI dominance are having the opposite effect — forcing Asian labs to build independent frontier capability faster than they otherwise would have.
items.key_fact: Multiple Asian startups shipping Mythos-comparable models during Anthropic export restrictions

items.title: GLM 5.2 Tops Claude on Semgrep's Cybersecurity Benchmarks
items.angle: A credible security tooling company's domain-specific eval shows a Chinese lab winning on the tasks that matter for AppSec — general leaderboards didn't predict this.
items.key_fact: GLM 5.2 outperforms Claude on Semgrep's cyber-specific benchmarks

items.title: Zyphra, Cohere, and Poolside Expand the Open Model Ecosystem
items.angle: With frontier closed models gated behind access tiers and export controls, open alternatives are becoming strategically important — not just ideologically preferred.
items.key_fact: Three companies simultaneously expanding open-weight model offerings

items.title: OpenAI Codex Still Can't Exclude Your .env Files
items.angle: A basic security feature — excluding sensitive files from AI context — remains an open GitHub issue. 172 likes on the issue says this isn't a niche complaint.
items.key_fact: Issue #2847 with 172 likes, still open — no .gitignore-style exclusion for Codex

items.title: llama.cpp Adds Native MiniCPM5 Tool Calling
items.angle: First-class function calling for MiniCPM5 in llama.cpp via autoparser — local models get tool-use parity without hacks.
items.key_fact: b9833 release adds XML tool call parser and PEG grammar support for MiniCPM5

items.title: Simon Willison's Guide to Productive Summer Hacking with AI
items.angle: Practical project selection and AI-assisted dev workflow advice from the person who ships more AI side projects than anyone in the community.
items.key_fact: Covers project scoping, AI tool selection, and workflow patterns for solo builders

items.title: 66 Game-Dev Agent Skills: A Template for Domain-Specific AI Skill Libraries
items.angle: The SKILL.md portable format and master router pattern isn't just for gamedev — it's a blueprint for packaging any domain expertise into agent-consumable units.
items.key_fact: 66 version-pinned skills covering Godot, Unity, Unreal, and web game engines

items.title: NanoEuler: GPT-2 From Scratch in Pure C/CUDA, No Frameworks
items.angle: In the tradition of Karpathy's nanoGPT — understand transformers at the metal level by building one without PyTorch as a safety net.
items.key_fact: Complete GPT-2 scale model in C/CUDA with zero framework dependencies
